records.title: Operation Everest II: Altitude Decompression Sickness During Repeated Altitude Exposure
records.locator: Abstract PDF p. 6; Results pp. 8–9; Table 2 p. 16; references 16 and 24 p. 14
records.evidence_note: The report and 1987 journal article have the same six authors, the same group of 23 investigators, and 28 episodes in 16 people with 37 recorded symptoms. The results text of the technical report gives 275 flights above 15,000 ft and 1,264.1 hours. Its abstract and Table 2 give 274 flights and 1,264.6 hours, which match the later journal results and detailed table. These are research investigators exposed repeatedly and eight separate experimental subjects do not supply a comparator for this analysis.

records.title: Altitude Decompression Sickness Incidence in the USAF
records.locator: March 1982 supplement, abstract 10, printed pp. 10–11 (PDF pp. 18–19) and footnote on p. 11
records.evidence_note: The main text describes 1 January 1978 to 31 December 1981, but the footnote specifies that the numbers in the abstract cover 1 January 1979 through 31 August 1981. The trainee and inside instructor-observer counts sum exactly to the overall figures. The authors report a twofold difference and p < 0.001. The crude count-based exposure rate ratio is 2.045. The later 1.7-fold citation in Wirjosemito et al. does not provide its source cells or separate dates. The trainee group included military aircrew and medical personnel as well as FAA-designated civilian trainees. The abstract does not give a military-only breakdown, unique-person counts, diagnostic criteria, role-specific treatment counts or site-level strata.
